headline: Open-source copies of OpenAI's dots agent are appearing while users report failures in the original.
score_reason: Pool 5, lowered 1: the underlying launch (4 Oct) is before 7 Oct (stale).
importance_line: It matters to people deciding whether to trust always-on agents, but the failure reports come from users and forum posts that OpenAI has not answered, so how widespread they are is unknown.
summary: The Register reports that OpenAI's dots, always-on AI agents first reported on 4 Oct 2026, are showing task failures, dropped connections and refusals, and that OpenAI did not reply to a request for comment. New today: free open-source copies, OpenDots from Tawkit (maker of the CopilotKit toolkit) and Open Dot by Prathit Joshi, a growth engineer at Composio, let people run similar agents with other AI models.
notes: Follow-up of 5 Oct edition C02-01 per follow_up_of. Date conflict between The Register and the pool flagged, not resolved.
